name: SQLAlchemy 2 async + asyncpg patterns
short_definition: Default Python data access for FastAPI services: SQLAlchemy 2.0 style (select(), Mapped annotations, DeclarativeBase) on create_async_engine(postgresql+asyncpg://...) with async_sessionmaker, request-scoped AsyncSession dependencies, explicit commit/rollback, and eager-loading discipline — not legacy Query API or sync sessions on the event loop.
scope_in: selectinload/joinedload; AsyncAttrs; stream() for large results
run_sync for rare sync-only metadata ops
scope_out: Pool sizing and PgBouncer details (see py-db-pool-lifecycle)
Alembic vs Supabase migration ownership (see py-migrations)
Django ORM / Tortoise / SQLModel deep alternatives
MySQL/SQLite async dialects as first-class defaults

defaults.models: DeclarativeBase + Mapped[] / mapped_column; AsyncAttrs mixin when lazy IO under async
defaults.sessions: async_sessionmaker(engine, expire_on_commit=False, class_=AsyncSession); one session per request via Depends yield
defaults.loading: Explicit selectinload/joinedload; no implicit lazy IO in async request handlers
defaults.transactions: async with session.begin() or explicit commit; rollback on exception in dependency finally
defaults.engine_lifecycle: Create engine in lifespan; await engine.dispose() on shutdown

use_when: Python service owns transactional multi-table writes
Complex joins, CTEs, or type-safe ORM graphs needed
Server-side service-role access to Postgres (incl. Supabase direct DB)
do_not_use_when: Browser/client path that should use Supabase JS + RLS only
Trivial single-table CRUD via PostgREST where supabase-py matches product SDK features
Ultra-hot path already proven faster in raw asyncpg and team accepts SQL-only

alternatives.asyncpg_raw: Max throughput / copy protocol; lose ORM
alternatives.sqlmodel: Thin Pydantic+SQLAlchemy layer — optional, still SQLAlchemy under the hood

do: Scope sessions to request; never share session across concurrent tasks
await session.execute / scalars; use stream for large sets
Eager-load relationships needed for response serialization
Map to Pydantic response models — don't return ORM instances from API
pool_pre_ping=True for long-lived workers; tune pool in py-db-pool-lifecycle
dont: Don't use sync create_engine / Session in async routes
Don't lazy-load relationships after session closed
Don't commit inside repositories and again in route without clear ownership
Don't open a new engine per request
Don't mix asyncio tasks that concurrently use one AsyncSession

code_skeleton:
from collections.abc import AsyncIterator
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from typing import Annotated

from fastapi import Depends, FastAPI
from sqlalchemy import String, select
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import (
    AsyncAttrs,
    AsyncSession,
    async_sessionmaker,
    create_async_engine,
)
from sqlalchemy.orm import DeclarativeBase, Mapped, mapped_column, selectinload

DATABASE_URL = "postgresql+asyncpg://user:pass@localhost:5432/app"

engine = create_async_engine(
    DATABASE_URL,
    pool_pre_ping=True,
    pool_size=5,
    max_overflow=10,
)
SessionLocal = async_sessionmaker(engine, expire_on_commit=False, class_=AsyncSession)

class Base(AsyncAttrs, DeclarativeBase):
    pass

class Item(Base):
    __tablename__ = "items"
    id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(primary_key=True)
    name: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(200))

async def get_session() -> AsyncIterator[AsyncSession]:
    async with SessionLocal() as session:
        try:
            yield session
            await session.commit()
        except Exception:
            await session.rollback()
            raise

SessionDep = Annotated[AsyncSession, Depends(get_session)]

@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(app: FastAPI):
    # optional: await conn.run_sync(Base.metadata.create_all) in tests only
    yield
    await engine.dispose()

app = FastAPI(lifespan=lifespan)

@app.get("/items/{item_id}")
async def get_item(item_id: int, session: SessionDep) -> dict:
    result = await session.execute(select(Item).where(Item.id == item_id))
    item = result.scalar_one_or_none()
    if item is None:
        return {"error": "not_found"}
    return {"id": item.id, "name": item.name}
failure_modes: MissingMissingGreenlet / await_only errors from implicit lazy load under async
Session used across concurrent tasks → race / interface error
Engine never disposed → connection leak on reload/k8s churn
N+1 queries under list endpoints without selectinload
DetachedInstanceError after commit with expire_on_commit=True default when reading attrs post-commit
Sync DBAPI calls blocking event loop
Transaction left open on cancelled request if dependency cleanup wrong
anti_patterns: Legacy Query API in new code
Global session = SessionLocal() at import used by all requests
ORM objects in FastAPI response_model without Pydantic
Agent scaffolding Flask-SQLAlchemy sync for new async services
select * patterns via Model load then Python filter for huge tables

versions_as_of.note: SQLAlchemy 2.0.x line; do not start greenfield on 1.4

config_snippets.alembic_env_hint: Use async engine in alembic/env.py with run_async + connection.run_sync(do_run_migrations)

deprecation_watch: databases (encode/databases) as default stack — prefer SQLAlchemy 2 async
ts_boundary: Next/TS uses Supabase JS or typed clients for user-scoped CRUD. Python SQLAlchemy for service jobs, multi-step transactions, AI pipelines writing DB. Share schema via migrations (one writer); regenerate TS types from Supabase/Postgres. Do not dual-write business invariants in Zod and ORM without DB constraints.
rust_boundary: Prefer sqlx/SQLx in Rust for latency-critical pure SQL services. Python SQLAlchemy when iteration speed and ORM graphs win. Same Postgres; avoid two ORMs thrashing schema without migration discipline.
supabase_boundary: Connect to Supabase Postgres direct (5432) or pooler per py-db-pool-lifecycle. Service role connection bypasses RLS — enforce authz in app for those paths. Prefer SET ROLE / request.jwt.claim patterns only when intentionally using RLS from backend. Migrations: pick Alembic OR supabase migrations, not both for same objects.
boundary_contracts: SQL constraints + RLS as source of truth for multi-tenant
OpenAPI does not expose internal ORM field dumps
Migration version table owned by one tool

decision_matrix_row.problem_class: Server-side Postgres access from Python services
decision_matrix_row.ts: Supabase client / Drizzle-or-Kysely if pure TS service
decision_matrix_row.rust: sqlx for typed SQL high-perf paths

threats: SQL injection via text() with f-strings
Service-role bypass of RLS without app authz
Over-fetch returning sensitive columns to API
mitigations: Bound parameters only; never format SQL with user input
Explicit authz checks when using bypass roles; audit service paths
Pydantic update models with explicit fields

must_not_generate: ORM returned directly as JSON without schema
implicit lazy loads for API graphs

tests_required: Repository/integration tests against real Postgres (testcontainers preferred)
Optional: migration upgrade head in CI
ci_gates: ban session.query( and create_engine( in async app paths
optional SQLAlchemy echo off in CI logs

negative: from sqlalchemy.orm import Session  # used in async route

Explicit loading; AsyncAttrs; no lazy IO surprises
Pydantic at HTTP edge; service-role RLS bypass must be intentional
